observations: The direction correction is confirmed against original publisher code, not inferred from the nearly symmetric stool silhouette. The immutable native_actions.py revision identified by inputs/source-rig.json uses S=0, E=+90, N=180, W=-90 degrees at line 468. Submitted and reopened evaluated root matrices now follow that convention for every named facing.

My prior round-02 review accepted four rotations without comparing their direction names to the original publisher. That contract conclusion was incorrect. This review checks the original source convention explicitly and does not rely on round-02 approval as evidence of correct direction labels.

All four current native PNGs and every packet preview were inspected directly. The blue padded seat keeps soft continuous corner and sidewall transitions, broad gentle shading, a distinct lower upholstered volume and clean separation from warm honey wood supports. Legs, crossbar, feet and open gaps remain readable at logical size and on light, gray and dark backgrounds.

The correction preserves the established appearance: independently decoded RGBA comparisons confirm new N equals old S, new E equals old W, new S equals old N, and new W equals old E. The corrected facing pixels also equal their corresponding reopened native renders. No visual regression, new seam, black dead patch, clipped corner, merged support or target halo was found.

Lighting stays horizontally neutral with no directional ground shadow. The repeated preview remains coherent at one-cell pitch. The source stool construction, slight crossbar-height distinction between N/S and E/W, and matte restrained material treatment are retained.
remainingDifferences: The selected target has stronger pillow inflation, brighter edge catches and richer fabric/wood texture. The candidate retains subtler padding and matte detail within the native geometry envelope and remains readable at intended size.
Target canvas placement, padding, changed proportions and colored silhouette fringe remain excluded from the criteria.
